intro: This is VERUS, running on a demonstration company: two manufacturers, three plants. The data is made up. The software is real.
01-sign-in: VERUS runs inside your network, and it only reads. It never changes a thing in your systems.
02-brief: Every morning, the plant manager gets a brief: what changed yesterday, and what needs a decision.
02b-show-me: Press Show me on any line, and VERUS lights up the numbers behind it.
03-finding: Each problem names the customer and the number: on-time delivery at seventy-five percent, against an eighty-five percent limit.
04-plan: VERUS proposes a plan, with the steps, who owns them, and the date it gets judged.
05-dashboard: Yesterday's numbers by line and department, with a caution wherever the data can't be trusted.
05b-verus-tour: New to a screen? Click VERUS, and he shows you around.
06-ask: Ask a question in plain words. VERUS answers, and shows exactly how it worked it out.
07a-sentence: Need something watched? Describe an agent in one sentence.
07b-agent: VERUS reads it back in plain words. Nothing runs until you switch it on.
08-backtest: First, it shows what the agent would have caught last year: here, the scrap spike on H B zero three in March.
09-documents: Your own documents answer too, with the page each answer came from.
10-owner: The owner sees every company side by side, on one set of definitions.
11-quiet: And hears when a key customer goes quiet: no contact in a hundred and seven days.
outro: VERUS. See it on your own data, read-only, inside your network.
